claims.text: Conventional CoCrFeNi struggles to maintain low friction and wear resistance from room temperature to 800 °C.
A controlled nanoscale precipitate dispersion in CoCrFeNi will create an adaptive nanohierarchical microstructure.
The precipitate-containing nanohierarchical structure will lower wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The precipitate-containing nanohierarchical structure will lower the coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
A thermal or alloying treatment can produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
B2 precipitates are a potentially suitable precipitate phase for the proposed CoCrFeNi intervention.
A nanohierarchical architecture can comprise intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The precipitates in the proposed architecture will be uniformly distributed.
At room temperature, the nanohierarchical structure provides multiple deformation pathways that release frictional stress in stages.
At 800 °C, the cooperative nanohierarchical structure activates a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer during wear.
The nanoscale precipitates specifically assist formation of the high-temperature glaze layer.
The dense nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear at 800 °C.
Adaptive friction-interface protection can provide very low wear rates over the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The proposed performance boundary applies to dry-air sliding from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under loads comparable to baseline tests.
